title: Raw minus fixed-size moth richness had a negative rainfall slope in one of four British samples in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested whether equal catch size changed the monthly rainfall slope for recorded moth richness. We used 685 selected trap-months from seven English and two Scottish sites in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015. Models controlled temperature, trap by month effects, sampling effort and linear time. Raw minus fixed-size richness had a rainfall slope of -4.34 taxa per 100 mm in later England, with a four-test interval of -8.56 to -0.11. The other three intervals included zero. The later English interval also included zero with trap trends or common traps. All four fixed-size richness intervals included zero. These results do not establish a common rainfall response. Catch size can reflect both real abundance and observation processes. Country weather, selected months, few Scottish sites and one monitoring archive limit inference. We test no air pollution effect, weather extreme or causal climate-change effect. The package contains code, source hashes, aggregate estimates, numerical checks and a figure. External source records and derived record tables remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Monthly rainfall slopes for raw richness, richness at 100 individuals, and their paired difference. Capped bars show ordinary 95 percent intervals; thin bars show four-test intervals.

citations.reason: Reuses the six pinned source files, selection design and adapted panel code. Tests rainfall slopes rather than warmth slopes. Records fully overlap.
Prior ECN study of nightly rain by temperature effects on catch. Different outcome and scale, shared monitoring network.
